body:
HELD-OUT SOURCE PREDECLARATION, BEFORE ANY MODEL EXECUTION.

Candidate: the complete narrative body of Chapter I, Down the Rabbit-Hole, from Lewis Carroll, Alices Adventures in Wonderland, first published 1865. Retrieval artifact: Project Gutenberg eBook 11 accessible plain text, Millennium Fulcrum Edition 3.0, updated 2025-06-26, credits Arthur DiBianca and David Widger. The currently retrieved raw artifact SHA-256 is 01b38ea4c710a84bc18d0bd41271a5a1a92b94e97b2812f4dece97d4a694725e.

Why this source, chosen without parser output: the full chapter naturally contains direct quotation, reported thought, short copular clauses, coordinated state change, fragment-like dialogue, and long nested sentences, while sharing essentially none of the WOG rule-stub vocabulary. It is narrative prose, not a Wikipedia convenience sample.

Repository posture: no Alice text is being committed in the contract slice. The runtime court should retrieve an exact external artifact, verify the raw checksum, apply one documented deterministic Chapter-I extraction and line-wrap/markup normalization, and record the derived checksum. If any bytes later enter git, docs/design/story-text-admission-checklist.md requires independent written sign-off first. The source record must name the 1865 edition basis, the specific Gutenberg transcription and credits, and every removal or normalization; Project Gutenberg web metadata alone is not being treated as that completed sign-off.

Freeze rule: the exact canonical derivation and resulting atlas sentence ledger must be reviewed and content-addressed before the first model run. If the chief rejects this source, the replacement must be named before freeze; it cannot be chosen after viewing WOG misses.
